name: changepoint_detection_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY/BANKNIFTY, large institutional TWAP/VWAP execution algorithms and macro news events generate persistent cumulative return deviations that build bar-by-bar before any lagging indicator confirms a trend. CUSUM (Cumulative Sum) control charts accumulate these micro-deviations against a 5-minute rolling baseline: the moment the positive CUSUM first crosses a volatility-scaled threshold, the index has entered a new buying regime where institutional demand is absorbing offers faster than the rolling mean. At 5-second resolution, we enter within the first 15-30 seconds of a new regime — before momentum strategies trigger and price moves further — riding the early continuation of the institutional order flow.

indicators.name: ret_1
indicators.purpose: 5-second bar return — the raw input to CUSUM accumulation. Not scaled from original (returns are returns regardless of bar size).

indicators.name: roll_mean_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute rolling baseline return. Original used 30-bar window on 1-min bars = 30-minute context, far too long for a 15-120s hold. 60 bars = 5 minutes captures the current intraday volatility regime without leaking session-open extremes into the baseline.

indicators.name: roll_std_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute rolling realized volatility — used to scale both CUSUM allowance (k) and detection threshold (h) dynamically. Makes CUSUM self-adjusting to different vol regimes during the day without VIX input.

indicators.name: cusum_pos
indicators.formula: max(0, cusum_pos[i-1] + ret_1[i] - roll_mean_60[i] - k_mult * roll_std_60[i]); reset to 0 on new session day
indicators.purpose: Accumulates positive excess returns above the allowable slack k. Once cusum_pos > h_mult * roll_std_60, a new uptrend regime is declared. Session-level reset prevents stale prior-session CUSUM contaminating new-day signals.

indicators.name: cusum_neg
indicators.formula: min(0, cusum_neg[i-1] + ret_1[i] - roll_mean_60[i] + k_mult * roll_std_60[i]); reset to 0 on new session day
indicators.purpose: Accumulates negative excess returns below the allowable slack. Mirrors cusum_pos for bearish regime detection.

conditions: cusum_pos[i] > h_mult * roll_std_60[i]  (positive CUSUM threshold crossed)
cusum_pos[i-1] <= h_mult * roll_std_60[i-1]  (just crossed — fresh break, not continuation)
buy_ce.confirmation: CUSUM crossed threshold for the first time in this run (cusum was at 0 within recent bars implying clean reset before the break)

conditions: abs(cusum_neg[i]) > h_mult * roll_std_60[i]  (negative CUSUM threshold crossed)
buy_pe.confirmation: Symmetric to buy_ce for bearish regime detection

exit.stop_rationale: NIFTY 30-second move is typically 2-5 option pts. If price immediately retraces 4 pts (~8 spot points at delta 0.5) after a CUSUM break, the regime signal was a false alarm (noise spike, not institutional flow). 4 pts gives one full typical move against us before stopping out.
exit.target_rationale: A genuine NIFTY regime change driven by institutional flow typically extends 10-20 spot points in the first 60-120 seconds (5-10 option pts). 6 pts captures ~60% of the median expected move, achieving 1:1.5 R:R which is profitable at 52%+ win rate.

filters.vix_filter: none — CUSUM threshold is dynamically volatility-scaled via roll_std_60; explicit VIX filter redundant
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:25 (need 60 bars for stable rolling statistics); no entries after 15:25
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume too noisy at 5s for reliable filtering
filters.trend_filter: none — CUSUM is itself the regime detector; no additional trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-medium — CUSUM from quality control (Page 1954) is rarely applied to 5-second financial data; the early detection before lagging indicators is genuine. Edge could decay if high-frequency algos adopt similar real-time CUSUM monitoring.

adaptation_notes: Original strategy traded NIFTY 50 constituent equities on 1-minute bars with a 30-minute rolling baseline (30 bars). For 5-second NIFTY index: (1) Rolling window compressed to 60 bars (5 min), NOT 360 bars (blind 12x) — at 5s the 5-min window captures the current intraday vol regime relevant to 15-120s holds. (2) Stock-specific filters (volume > 1.5x ADV, earnings filter, bid-ask spread < 5 bps) all dropped — NIFTY index is continuously liquid and does not have earnings days. (3) Trend filter ('NIFTY 50 must not have opposing changepoint') inverted into the strategy itself — we ARE trading NIFTY directly. (4) Position sizing removed — standard ₹1L capital per entry. (5) k and h multipliers made tunable since the original's k=0.5*sigma, h=4*sigma were calibrated on equities; index returns have different autocorrelation structure.
weaknesses: CUSUM assumes a step-function shift in mean return; NIFTY regime shifts during high-freq periods can be gradual (ramping), causing cusum to cross threshold late after most of the move has occurred
At 5-second resolution, microstructure noise can trigger false CUSUM breaks — the 'just crossed' filter helps but cannot eliminate all noise-driven crossings
Session-level CUSUM reset means early-session signals (09:25-09:35) fire before sufficient history accumulates, potentially lower quality
